#1 I don't know whether this is the right place to post this.

The claims at irreducible topological space are not quite correct. According to the definition given there, the empty set is irreducible (it cannot be written as the union of two proper closed subsets). However, if the empty set is irreducible, then it's not true that the only irreducible subsets of sober spaces are the closures of single points, since then the empty set is also irreducible, and it's not the closure of any point.

Hence I propose the following fix: Take an unbiased definition of the word irreducible: A space is irreducible if it cannot written as a finite union of proper closed subsets. This agrees with the previous definition, except that it makes the empty set be not irreducible.
